solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hang together, present company to go first

indicators.note: to go first tells us the company piece is placed before the present piece

parts.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for company, as in a firm's name
present, as in in attendance, means here

explanation.surface: Someone asks the people in the room to stick together and lead the way.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to stick together or be united, the same as hanging together.

clue.text: Change name in secret

indicators.note: in means the name letter goes inside the secret word

parts.note: covert means secret

explanation.surface: Someone changes their name secretly.
explanation.definitionFit: To convert something is to change it into another form.

clue.text: Erratic fellow loses head over wager

indicators.note: loses head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: chap means fellow
to hazard is to wager or gamble

explanation.surface: A wild man loses his mind over a bet.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Haphazard means random or without order, so erratic.

clue.text: Often a positive factor in man and monkey

definitions.text: Often a positive factor in man
definitions.meaning: refers to the blood factor most people test positive for
the macaque species in which the blood factor was discovered

explanation.surface: Something common to man and monkey is usually a good thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rhesus factor in blood is named after the rhesus macaque; most humans are Rh-positive.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rh blood antigen, usually present, and the macaque it was named after.

clue.text: First one a German locked up long, long ago

indicators.note: locked up means the letters sit enclosed within the words First one a German

explanation.surface: A tale of the first person, a German, imprisoned in ancient times.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside firST ONE A GErman, held by 'locked up'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stone Age is the prehistoric period, a time very long ago.

clue.text: Swarm heads off towards Europe every minibreak

indicators.note: heads off means taking the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Tourists flock to Europe on every short holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To teem is to be crowded with moving creatures, much as a swarm is.

clue.text: Beginner one trained to box, say

indicators.note: trained suggests the letters of one are put into a new order
say means the word for boxing is taken by its sound

parts.note: to box is to fight

explanation.surface: A novice is coached in the art of boxing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trained' turns ONE into NEO, and 'say' gives PHYTE, sounding like FIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A neophyte is a new convert or novice, someone just starting out.

clue.text: Outsider who has a right to property

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep someone's property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: Asking whether a stranger has a legal claim to some land.
explanation.definitionFit: An alien is a foreigner or stranger, someone from outside.

clue.text: Avoids church going in multiple directions

indicators.note: going in means the church letters go inside the directions

parts.note: E, S, E, W, S are compass directions

explanation.surface: Someone shuns a church by heading every which way.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew something is to deliberately keep away from it.

clue.text: Seems to be the last place you would visit!

definitions.text: Seems to be the last place you would visit!

parts.words: Seems to be the last place you would visit!
parts.note: alludes to the saying 'see this Italian city and die', so it would be the final place on your travels

explanation.surface: A traveller remarks that some place seems the least appealing destination imaginable.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests somewhere nobody wants to go; the saying 'See Naples and die' makes it literally the last place you visit.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says one should see this Italian city and then die, as nothing could surpass it.

clue.text: Diabolical alternative comedian

indicators.note: alternative signals a different arrangement of the letters of comedian

explanation.surface: A fiendish alternative stand-up comic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternative comedian' reads as a style of comedy, but 'alternative' is the anagram signal on COMEDIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Demoniac means possessed by or like a demon, so devilish or diabolical.

clue.text: Way tenor becomes man with loudest voice

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: becomes signals the letters of tenor turning into a new form

explanation.surface: How a tenor develops into the man with the most powerful voice.
explanation.walkthrough: Stentor was a Greek herald in the Iliad whose voice was as loud as fifty men's.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek herald in Homer was famed for an enormous voice, hence the word stentorian.

clue.text: Send to the country girl with acute jitters

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name

indicators.note: jitters suggests nervous shaking, so the letters of acute are jumbled

explanation.surface: A nervous girl is sent off to the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Second World War children were evacuated from cities to the country, which makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: To evacuate people is to remove them from danger, as wartime evacuees were sent from cities to rural areas.

clue.text: Moan and moan about the end of smoking

indicators.note: about means the moan piece goes around the other letter

parts.note: to moan is to whine

indicators.note: the end of picks the last letter of smoking

explanation.surface: A smoker complains repeatedly about having to give up cigarettes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The end of' takes G from smoking, and 'about' puts WHINE around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To whinge is a British informal word for complaining persistently, i.e. to moan.

clue.text: Meat supplier takes ages to supply traditional pie filling

parts.note: a pig supplies pork and bacon
eons are ages

explanation.surface: A farmer takes a long time providing for an old-fashioned pie.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigeon pie is an old British dish, so the birds are a traditional filling.

clue.text: Ancestral hall on River Bank, not found in Ireland

definitions.meaning: points to the owner of ... Hall, the riverside home in The Wind in the Willows
this amphibian is said to be absent from Ireland, like snakes

explanation.surface: A stately home by a riverbank, unlike anything in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Toad Hall is the family seat of Mr Toad in Kenneth Grahame's The Wind in the Willows, set by the River Bank. The second sense is shaky: the natterjack does live in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Toad is the master of Toad Hall, and the common amphibian is reputedly missing from Ireland.

clue.text: Stop crying, as children's fights are apt to do

definitions.text: as children's fights are apt to do

parts.note: to stop is to end
crying means in tears

explanation.surface: A parent's remark that squabbling children tend to finish up weeping.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for finishing badly or unhappily, as children's squabbles often do.

clue.text: One checks on University Hospital for the Economist

parts.note: A is one
dams check or hold back water
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Someone checks on a university hospital for a business magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Economist' poses as the magazine, but it is the Scottish economist who wrote The Wealth of Nations.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighteenth-century Scot is seen as the father of modern economics.

clue.text: A force crossed the river, all paid for

parts.note: to ford is to cross a river by wading

explanation.surface: An army crosses a river with all costs covered.
explanation.definitionFit: Something afforded has had its cost met, so it was paid for.

clue.text: Comfortable situation needs flowers, not nails

definitions.meaning: an easy, pleasant state of affairs
a literal bed of blooms, as opposed to a fakir's bed of nails

explanation.surface: Advice that comfort requires blooms rather than spikes.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally as a flowerbed, contrasted with the bed of nails an Indian fakir lies on.
explanation.definitionFit: Life is no such bed when it is hard; the idiom means an easy, pleasant situation.

clue.text: Thanksgiving that requires British meat, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means one letter of the meat word is lost, here the first

parts.note: venison is deer meat

explanation.surface: A Thanksgiving dinner needs British meat for most of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thanksgiving' suggests the American holiday, but here it means a blessing. 'Mostly' drops V from VENISON, leaving ENISON.
explanation.definitionFit: A benison is a blessing or benediction, a giving of thanks.

clue.text: Money required to swap cold for hot food

indicators.note: C (cold) and H (hot) are tap abbreviations, and the C in the money word is replaced with H

parts.note: cash is money

explanation.surface: Cash is needed to trade cold food for a hot meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot food' looks like one phrase, but 'hot' belongs to the swap and 'food' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hash is a dish of chopped cooked meat and vegetables, a kind of food.

clue.text: Ancient man's brief clothing discovered inside trough

indicators.note: inside means the clothing goes within the trough

parts.note: a hod is a trough for carrying bricks
a mini is a short skirt

explanation.surface: A caveman's skimpy outfit turns up in a feeding trough.
explanation.definitionFit: A hominid is a member of the human family, including early ancestors of man.

clue.text: Factory needs one to be flexible

indicators.note: needs means the factory takes in the one letter

parts.note: a plant is a factory
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A factory requires a single worker who can be adaptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliant means easily bent, so supple or flexible.

clue.text: A posh car, in at the moment, can be cramped

indicators.note: in means the car pieces go inside the word for at the moment

parts.note: at the moment means now
RR stands for Rolls-Royce, a luxury car

explanation.surface: A luxury car, fashionable just now, can be a tight fit inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow means of small width, so cramped or confined.

clue.text: Parts of film showing folk dances

explanation.surface: Sections of a movie depicting traditional dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinema film comes on spools, and Scottish country dances share the name.

clue.text: Masculine version doesn't need one in the US

indicators.note: version suggests a new form of the remaining letters
doesn't need means the letter for one is removed from masculine

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A male edition of something that is unnecessary in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doesn't need one' removes I from MASCULINE, and 'version' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Sam is the personification of the United States government.

clue.text: A Russian, say, has to toil endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to slave is to toil

explanation.surface: A Russian has to work without a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Russians are an example of the Slavic peoples of eastern Europe.

clue.text: Prodigal son's gloom about death

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son

indicators.note: about means the gloom word goes around the death word

parts.note: a pall is a dark cloud of gloom
death is one's end

explanation.surface: The Prodigal Son feels a gloom about dying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prodigal son' reads as the parable, but 'Prodigal' alone is the definition and 'son' gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: A spendall is a spendthrift, someone wastefully extravagant, i.e. prodigal.

clue.text: Slander an African country's good name

parts.note: Mali is a West African country

explanation.surface: Defaming a nation in Africa's reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: To malign is to speak evil of someone, so to slander them.

clue.text: One side crazily welcomes very steep fall

indicators.note: welcomes means the jumbled letters take another letter inside
crazily signals the letters of one side being jumbled

explanation.surface: One faction wildly embraces a sharp decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazily' turns ONESIDE into NOSEDIE, which 'welcomes' V.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosedive is a steep downward plunge, of an aircraft or of prices.

clue.text: Being tied up, topless, may get you irritated!

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: hitched means tied up or fastened

explanation.surface: A risqué remark about being bound up and unclothed causing itching.
explanation.definitionFit: If skin has itched it has been irritated, prompting a scratch.
